subject: Coordination: Offboarding playbook, notice timing & SLA handback for Glyph Health
body:
From: Elaine Wong <elaine.wong@glyphhealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@glyphhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:02:14 -0700
Subject: Offboarding — timeline, notice & credits question

Hi Sean,

Quick question as we evaluate renewing vs. sunsetting one of our pilots: what notice window do you require for termination for convenience, and can you outline how pro-rated credits/refunds are calculated for prepaid committed capacity? Procurement also asked for an offboarding checklist so we can budget the operational handover.

If we need to push through an early unwind, having clear SLA handback (S3 export, log retention, support hours) will help legal and security sign-off.

Thanks,
Elaine
Elaine Wong
Director, Infrastructure Programs
Glyph Health

-----

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Wong <elaine.wong@glyphhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Offboarding — timeline, notice & credits question

Elaine — thanks for the note. Short answers up front: we typically have a 30‑day notice for termination for convenience on hosted contracts, but we can be flexible on the notice window and refund mechanics for pilots if procurement needs 60 days.

Attached is a concise offboarding checklist and a first-pass redline of the MSA that calls out:
- Auto‑renew opt-out procedure and notice timing
- Pro‑rata refund calculation for prepaid reserved capacity (refund-matrix.xlsx)
- Data export SLA (export package within X business days; logs retained for Y days)

I’ll loop Karthik and Olga for legal language — if you can confirm the 60‑day ask, we’ll propose compromise wording (60‑day notice for non‑renewal; 30‑day notice preserved for termination-for-convenience with limited operational credits).

Attachments: [offboarding-checklist.pdf] [redline-MSA-draft.docx] [refund-matrix.xlsx]

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

-----

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Elaine Wong <elaine.wong@glyphhealth.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 10:08:22 -07:00
Subject: RE: Offboarding — timeline, notice & credits question

Elaine — appreciate the context. From a legal standpoint we want to keep termination-for-convenience narrow to avoid operational disruption: proposed draft preserves a 30‑day written notice coupled with a 30‑day wind‑down period. For pilots, we can add an Order Form amendment that:

- Allows Glyph to provide 60 days notice to avoid out-of-cycle charges;
- Caps refunds to unused committed capacity (pro‑rata by day) excluding any usage-based fees already consumed;
- Requires a written acceptance of the offboarding plan 15 days before final cutover to confirm export details.

I attached a redline with bracketed language where we’d expect procurement to confirm (lines marked /*PROCU MARGIN*/).

—Karthik
Sr. Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

-----

From: Elaine Wong <elaine.wong@glyphhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Sep 2026 08:40:03 -07:00
Subject: RE: Offboarding — timeline, notice & credits question

Thanks Karthik — that sounds reasonable. Procurement’s preference is:
- 60‑day notice for non‑renewal triggers (so we can align budget cycles);
- For termination for convenience, we’re OK with 30‑day notice but need clearer language that any prepaid reserved capacity will be refunded pro‑rata on unused days (we’ll need the exact formula to insert into our finance system).

On exports: can you confirm S3 export will include model logs and the last 90 days of request/response logs? We’ll need that documented in the amendment before legal will sign.

Elaine

-----

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Wong <elaine.wong@glyphhealth.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Sep 2026 11:07:55 -07:00
Subject: RE: Offboarding — timeline, notice & credits question

Elaine — quick clarifications from security/legal: we can commit to the S3 export containing customer-provided content, standard request/response logs and any platform-level metadata we store; we need to keep a shorter retained copy of full debug traces due to internal retention policy, but we will export the last 90 days of request/response logs as requested.

I’ve updated the redline to:
- Specify export format (gzipped JSON bundle) and delivery timeframe (10 business days after accepted offboarding plan);
- Add a limited SLA handback credit schedule if we fail to meet export SLA (see refund-matrix.xlsx);
- Add a clause that reserved-capacity refunds are calculated pro‑rata on unused full days and exclude committed minimums already consumed.

If procurement confirms the 60‑day non‑renewal window, I’ll mark the amendment and create a DocuSign envelope with the revised Order Form clauses.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Senior Contracts Counsel
Redwood Inference

-----

From: James Carter <james.carter@glyphhealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Elaine Wong <elaine.wong@glyphhealth.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@glyphhealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2026 11:18:30 -07:00
Subject: RE: Offboarding — timeline, notice & credits question

Folks — procurement confirms we need the 60‑day non‑renewal window tied to fiscal close (that’s our hard ask). We appreciate the flex on the termination-for-convenience refund mechanics — please include the exact pro‑rata formula in the refund-matrix.xlsx so our FP&A can ingest it.

Next steps from our side: once we get the DocuSign amendment, we’ll route it through procurement and finance (2–3 business days). Could Redwood also attach an example export package so our infra team can validate restore/ingest?

Thanks,
James Carter
Procurement Manager
Glyph Health

-----

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Wong <elaine.wong@glyphhealth.com>, James Carter <james.carter@glyphhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2026 14:35:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Offboarding — timeline, notice & credits question

Great — thanks James. Plan of record:
1) Redwood legal (Olga/Karthik) to finalize MSA redline and Order Form amendment reflecting: 60‑day non‑renewal window; 30‑day termination‑for‑convenience wind‑down; pro‑rata refund formula (as documented in refund-matrix.xlsx); 10 business day export SLA for last 90 days of request/response logs.
2) Olga to generate DocuSign envelope for the Order Form amendment by EOD tomorrow.
3) Sean to upload an example gzipped export bundle to a secure share for Glyph infra to validate ingest (ETA 48 hours after DocuSign sent).
4) Procurement to sign the amendment and confirm billing/pricing acceptance (James/Elaine).

I’ll follow up with the DocuSign link and the secure share URL when ready. Appreciate the collaborative give-and-take here — we’ll aim to preserve predictability for both legal and operations.

Best,
Sean
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: offboarding-checklist.pdf]
